classification.habit: Erect perennial undershrub, 0.5–1.5 m tall, covered with soft stellate hairs.
classification.habitat: Waste places, roadsides and open dry ground in the plains.
classification.distribution: Throughout tropical and subtropical India, ascending to about 1,000 m.

identification.description: Subshrub with cylindrical taproot, cordate velvety leaves and yellow solitary flowers; seeds are characteristic.
identification.whole_plant: Erect, velvety undershrub with cordate leaves and small yellow axillary flowers.
identification.root: Long, cylindrical, woody, pale yellowish-brown, with few lateral roots; mucilaginous and slightly sweet.
identification.stem: Erect, terete, woody below and branched, covered with stellate hairs.
identification.leaf: Simple, alternate, cordate-ovate, 2.5–5 cm long, crenate-serrate, softly hairy on both surfaces.
identification.flower: Solitary or clustered, axillary, small, yellow, on short pedicels jointed near the top.
identification.fruit: Schizocarp of 8–10 mericarps, each with two long awns.
identification.seed: Small, reniform, dark brown to black, smooth.

therapeutics.precautions: Contains ephedrine-type alkaloids; use cautiously in hypertension, heart disease, anxiety, insomnia and glaucoma, and with stimulant or MAO-inhibitor drugs.
therapeutics.contraindications: Avoid concentrated extracts in uncontrolled hypertension, cardiac arrhythmia and thyrotoxicosis; avoid in Kapha-predominant Ama states.

shlokas:
बलाचतुष्टयं शीतं मधुरं बलकान्तिकृत्।
स्निग्धं ग्राहि समीरास्रपित्तास्रक्षतनाशनम्॥

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: Sida cordifolia contains ephedrine-type and quinazoline alkaloids, with the highest concentration in the seeds.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Improves strength and stamina, useful in vata disorders and nervous weakness.
modern_information.safety_notes: Traditional preparations are generally well tolerated; ephedrine content means extracts can raise blood pressure and heart rate.
